usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/language-detect?text=<urlencoded text>&min_length=<optional int> (no body; params in query string)

inputExample.text: Hello, how are you doing today?

usage.outputShape: body.language_code, body.language_name, body.confidence, body.script_detected, body.text_length, body.alternatives[] (each {language_code, language_name, confidence})
quirks: GET with query params only — pass 'text' as a URL-encoded query parameter, there is no request body.
Optional 'min_length' query param (default 10) sets minimum text length for reliable detection.

Detection accuracy is weak in practice: a clear English sentence was misclassified as 'sot' (Sotho) with the correct language not even in the top alternatives. Treat confidence/language_code as low-trust; backend uses the 'franc' trigram library (see _meta.provenance.source).
language_name often equals the raw ISO code (e.g. 'sot', 'zyb', 'nob') rather than a human-readable name; only some codes resolve to friendly names.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.strale.io/x402/language-detect with the text URL-encoded in the 'text' query parameter (e.g. ?text=Bonjour%20le%20monde); optionally add &min_length=N. Payment is x402 USDC on Base, ~$0.02 per call, settled synchronously — the 200 response IS the result. Read the detected language from body.language_code / body.language_name with body.confidence, and body.alternatives[] for ranked guesses. Note the detection accuracy is unreliable, so do not depend on its output for critical routing.
